## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR shouldn't merge yet. The new `Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them, but the class comment at `app/cache.py:14-15` says every path into `_store` lower-cases the key. As a result, any key with an uppercase letter can't be read back. The DEFAULT_TTL change and its comment match each other.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` writes `self._store[key]` using the key as given, but `get` looks up and deletes `key.lower()`. So after `c.set("Alpha", 1)`, both `c.get("Alpha")` and `c.get("alpha")` return `None`. This breaks the rule in `app/cache.py:14-15`: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". Could you change line 27 to `self._store[key.lower()] = ...`? `test_set_then_get_round_trip` (tests/test_cache.py:10-14) only ever sets the all-lowercase `"alpha"`, so it can't catch this. Adding a case like `c.set("Alpha", 1); assert c.get("alpha") == 1` would. — Callers who set any key with an uppercase letter get silent cache misses. Their entries also stay in `_store` forever, because `get` only deletes the lower-cased key on expiry. That's an unbounded memory leak for the callers this PR moves off direct `_store` access.
